properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2023 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Howe Twp, Forest county. 78.66(c) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to properly report and describe a reportable release of brine by telephone, including pertinent information on: name, address and telephone number of the company and person reporting the incident, date & time of the incident or when it was detected, location and cause of the incident, quantity of brine released, impacts to soil, groundwater or surface water, and remedial actions.

Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: 78.66(c) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to properly report and describe a reportable release of brine by telephone, including pertinent information on: name, address and telephone number of the company and person reporting the incident, date & time of the incident or when it was detected, location and cause of the incident, quantity of brine released, impacts to soil, groundwater or surface water, and remedial actions.
Violation ID: 995088
Permit API: 053-29526
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-14 to Dorso Lp in New Stanton Boro, Westmoreland county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-14
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 877203
Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to a notification received by the Department from the operator of plugging being conducted at this site. Assisting with this inspection is WQS Eric Norman. Conditions on site are cloudy, light snow on the ground, and approximately 30 degrees. The access road appears rutted with several locations that have standing water present. One such location (Photo 1-3) has what appears to be an outfall basin where two streams meet and then pass under the access road via a culvert heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. It appears that at this location some sediment laden water may have left the road in the vicinity of the hay bales (Photo 1), went down slope and discharged into this basin. At the time of this inspection it does not appear to be currently ongoing. The straw bale barriers at this location do not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 990059
Permit API: 015-20451
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/30/2023
Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. It was 28 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. There were water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall on the pad surface. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.There were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment. A gas compressor is on site but was not running during the inspection.Three piles of excavated material from the Chesapeake Grippo well site are temporarily being stored on location until being approved for disposal. Each pile was staged in plastic-lined secondary containment. I field tested water puddles and soil around the perimeter of each excavation pile with the following results: The highest reading was on the north side of the south pile which was from a 1' x 8' water puddle outside the edge of the secondary containment that field tested at 3.04 mS conductance. Other water puddles around the perimeter of the south pile field tested at 0.7 mS conductance or less. Water puddles on the east side and west side of the two north piles field tested at 0.5 mS conductance. Water puddles along the north side of the two north piles field tested at 0.4 mS conductance or less. Water puddles south of the northwest pile field tested at 0.5 mS conductance or less. There were no water puddles south of the northeast pile. I field tested the soil south of the northeast pile with results at 0.7 mS conductance or less.No violations were noted during the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3524618 for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface in proximity to stockpiles of contaminated excavated waste.The DEP recommends the following:1. Remove the piles of excavated material as soon as the waste is approved for disposal.2. After removing the piles of excavated materials and secondary containment, screen the site for possible contamination and clean/report as necessary.I left the site at 1130 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted and INCIDENT inspection of the SWEPI LP - Kennedy 137 well pad located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 4/15/2019 @1000 hours the weather was 43 degrees, rain, winds W 18mph. Approximately 0.6 inches of precipitation was received over the past 24 hours. On 4/14/2019 @1700 hours, Shell representatives called in a spill of a reported 90 BBLs of production fluid to the pad surface of the Kennedy 137. A truck driver had discovered a hose connected to one of the Highland production tanks that was discharging production fluid to the pad surface. The driver assumed the Highland tank was at maximum capacity when it discharged it's contents. Mr. Bernethy, SWEPI Environmental Coordinator, contacted the WQS this morning to state the driver was mistaken. The Highland tank was not at capacity and the revised amount of the spill is 3-4 BBLs. Mr. Bernethy stated the spill was estimated to have impacted ~300-400 square feet of pad surface. As of yesterday evening, a vac truck had removed standing fluid from the pad surface,and a sump was constructed below the discharge valve from the Highland tank to remove accumulated fluid. Mr. Bernethy stated the sump will be regularly monitored and fluid removed as needed. As of today's inspection, no personnel were observed onsite. The impacted area below the Highland tank was observed flagged with cones and spray paint. The constructed sump was observed, and the fluid being held had a field measured conductivity of 1.00 mS/cm. All other puddles screened on the pad surface had a field measured conductivity of <1.0mS/cm. The fluid in the E&S channel below the fill slope was screened and found to be <1.0mS/cm. The E&S trap below the fill slope was also screened and found to be <1.0mS/cm. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time do to the reported release of 3-4 barrels of production fluid to the pad surface: CSL402b Potential Pollution SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids. We departed the site @ 1100 hours.

Comments: On January 25 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Fatur Well Pad after a Department OGI requested a follow up in regards to a pink oily substance observed on the pad.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The ERP and PPC plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible leaks. Upon inspection of the GPU, there appeared to be a red tinted fluid in the containment surrounding the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and revealed elevated readings of 4.39mS. Upon further inspection, there appeared to be a disconnected hose and red tinted fluid on the gravel behind the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken from the surface on the ground beneath the puddles on the well pad and indicated elevated readings of 1.08mS and 1.37mS in comparison to the background reading of 0.12 mS taken from the surface of the soil along the well site perimeter. Directly adjacent to the GPU was a container with red colored fluid labeled as gear lubricant. The Department recommends the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with Department standards. The Department requests clarification on what the red tinted fluid observed on the ground is and how much was released with in 10 days of receiving this report.Upon inspecting the additional production equipment onsite, there appeared to be oil based matter being absorbed by cloths beneath the compressor. There did not appear to be any staining on the ground surrounding the compressor. The Department recommends the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in the proper manner to prevent any future pollution events. Upon inspection of the area mentioned by an OGI to have a pink oily matter on the ground, it appeared that a majority of the substance may have been washed away by recent rain as only small spots of a pink colored matter was observed on the ground surrounding a production tank next to the compressor. Conductivity readings were taken on the ground where the pink substance was observed and did not indicate elevated reading with readings of 0.13mS and 0.11mS. Upon inspection of the production tank and containment, the pink oily fluid was observed. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and did not indicate elevated readings with a reading of 0.09mS. The Department requests information regarding what was released and how much was released in this area with in 10 days of receipt of this report. The Department recommends removing excess fluids from secondary containments in order to ensure they meet required holding capacities of 110% according to Chapter 78a64a.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the release observed near the GPU, failure to have the gear lubricant in proper secondary containment, and the secondary containment for the production tank near the compressor failing to meet proper storage capacity. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

Comments: On July 15, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of a reported spill from production fluid tank secondary containment. The Department met with Nathan Harris from Pennsylvania General Energy and discussed how the hole occurred. PGE estimated about 2-3 barrels were spilled from the containment of the production fluid tanks secondary containment. At the time of inspection, the impacted soil had been excavated below 2,500 uS/cm. The area impacted was about 20' x 15' and about 5 inches of soil in the area has been removed. Moody and Associates were delineating the area and collecting soil samples. The impacted area was limited to the pad surface. Thus, due to the presence of produced water mixed with stormwater and the reported volume of the release,the remediation under Act 2 is required under 78a.66(c).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/30/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 1000297
Permit API: 081-21944
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/30/2023
Comments: A routine inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions. A Precision Drilling rig is still in operation on the well pad. I first looked at the trench along the side of the well site secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the trench was 764 uS/cm. A sheen was observed on the surface near the ramp over for the backyard area which appeared consistent with an iron-reducing bacteria sheen. Company man Pat Smith walked over to me while I was looking at the trench and told me that there had just been a release of a base oil to the pad surface next to the upright base oil tanks. We walked over to the base oil tanks and I saw an area of fluid on the pad surface immediately adjacent to the secondary containment for the base oil tanks. The area was approximately 30 ft by 10 ft. Mr. Smith said that the estimated volume of the release was 20 gallons. The electrical conductivity of the fluid was 1.0 uS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter. Mr. Smith said that Tobias Excavation was on the way to scrape up the impacted pad material. On July 2, 2023 EQT representative Rick Hall sent an email to the Department which included a document which detailed the remediation of the base oil release. The report included the volume of material excavated, 8 tons, the dimensions of the pad that was scraped, 20 ft wide by 40 ft long by 6 ft deep, as well as photos of the area during excavation and after the area was backfilled with new gravel. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On 02/03/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 0915 hours, weather was 33F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently drilled wells located onsite which are currently undergoing flow back as a result of the completion of hydraulic fracturing activities; well permits are posted with the Act 9 sign at the site entrance (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are not yet in use but are held in a secondary containment structure. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the tanks are not yet labeled, and I discussed the need to label them with personnel onsite; they informed me that they would be labeled after they dried off. Two modular aboveground storage structures (MASS's) are located onsite to hold brine during flow back, and a lined residual waste container is located next to them and held on containment (photo #5). Multiple upright brine and temporary storage tanks for holding produced fluids during flow back are also noted onsite; all tanks are held in secondary containment which appears to be functioning as intended (photos #6 and 7).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review at the site entrance and is up to date (photo #8). One infiltration basin serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photo #9). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control it appears to be functioning as intended.The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No violations noted. I departed the site at 1015 hours.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 04/01/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Ralph Babcock onsite. We traveled the area of the impact together. There are still two 24/7 water trucks onsite actively recovering fluids. Fluids above the release point were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~1080 us/cm (1 us/cm = 0.001 mS/cm) (photo #2). Those fluids continued traveling through the stormwater ditch into the active sumps (photo #3 and 4). They have excavated up to feet of material was removed from the ditch. The EC of fluids within the sump #1 and 2 was ~1.2 mS/cm. At that time Repsol instructed the truck operator to move his hoses below the sumps to start recovering those fluids which measured ~3.10 mS/cm (photo #5). The EC of the fluids that were directly entering the stormwater basin were ~540 us/cm. The stormwater basin has a containment in place (photo #7). Fluids were being recovered on top of and below the containment. ~60 barrels had been recovered today from the stormwater basin and sump #3. The EC of the fluids directly downgrade of the stormwater basin outlet and before sump #3 was ~5.1 mS/cm. The EC of fluids located below sump #3 was ~6.38 mS/cm. Brow/black vegetation was observed in that area (photo #11 and 12). We traveled downstream and the EC of the fluids were ~1.4 mS/cm. A spring intercepted the path of the flow from above grade. The EC of the fluids downstream of the spring was ~1.2-1.4 mS/cm. The EC of the marsh area was ~1.5 mS/cm. The EC of the UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the impacts was 25.3 us/cm (0.0253 mS/cm). Fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek at the upper confluence were field measured for EC at 2.4-2.7mS/cm (photo #18). From the upper confluence of the impact to the wetland inflow EC was 185.9- 225 us/cm (0.1859 -0.225 mS/cm) (photo #19). The EC of fluids from the UNT Rockwell Creek downstream impact was 379 us/cm.Repsol stated the stimulation activities for API #015-23994, 23995, 23996, 23997 and 23998 are scheduled to begin on 04/16/2026. Violations against API #015-23994 remain open at this time. I departed at 1100 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/16/2022 to PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in Ridgway Twp, Elk county. 78a59b(g) - WELL DEVELOPMENT IMPOUNDMENTS - Operator failed to properly restore the impoundment within 9 months of completion of hydraulic fracturing of the last well serviced by the impoundment.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/16/2022
Violation Code: 78a59b(g) - WELL DEVELOPMENT IMPOUNDMENTS - Operator failed to properly restore the impoundment within 9 months of completion of hydraulic fracturing of the last well serviced by the impoundment.
Violation ID: 948138
Permit API: 047-24586
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Ridgway Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 8/21/2011. There is a second active well (047-24580) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 7/20/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0021 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. A well development impoundment (Impoundment # 5) is located approximately 900’ northeast of the HM1 well site. This impoundment is covered by the same ESCGP that encompasses the HM1 well site. The impoundment has not yet been restored, and greater than nine months have passed since the last well was serviced by this impoundment. The Department does not have record showing that this well development impoundment has been registered, as is required by Chapter 78a.59b(b). The water from this impoundment is currently being discharged via a 2" plastic pipe out of the southwest corner of the impoundment onto a vegetated swale. There are currently no surface concerns evident from this dewatering. The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road to prevent potential E&S issues. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

Comments: At the time of inspection, meet with Chris McNichols ( Big Dog Energy LLC). Label affixed to well with Permit No. 37-019-21988 (Photo 1). Inspection Date: 4/13/2026
Comments: On April 13, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-396434) at the Ritter well site in Redstone Township, Fayette County. The purpose of this inspection was to conduct further on-site review. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on July 10, 2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of Tree Farm road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in an accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). Tree Farm Road is a township gravel road that connects to the site access road. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on site (photo 2). Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production. Well 5H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 17). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the gas wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the GPU units (photos 16 and 18).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 4 and 19).The severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation remains downslope of the well pad on Tree Farm Road (photos 10-13). The Department observed a rock-lined stormwater channel along the access road, which is located upslope of Tree Farm Road. This rock-lined stormwater channel appears to be in need of maintenance, as it appears to be nearly level with the access road (photo 6). Vegetation that appears to be flattened by recent stormwater washout was observed downslope of the rock-lined stormwater channel and access road (photo 5). An erosion channel obscured by vegetation was found within the well site boundary upslope of the most severely eroded portion of Tree Farm Road (photo 14). This erosion channel appears to pose the potential to encourage channelized stormwater flow downslope to Tree Farm Road.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for failure to conduct long-term maintenance on Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMPs), which appear to be discharging excess stormwater to Tree Farm Road and resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Transmittal of this inspection report was delayed due to an IT error.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 838323
Permit API: 081-20658
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cummings Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-07
Comments: On January 7, 2019, Department representatives Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of the reported spill on PGE Company LLC. Moore Rd. Ext. The Department met Chris Earley and Chad Oechler with PGE. A tanker truck was hauling production fluids from COP Tract 729 Pad E, as the truck was driving down the access road a valve failed on the tank. This caused about 2-3 barrels of production fluid to spill on Moore Rd. Ext. The tanker truck also spilled about 10 gallons on COP Tract 729 Pad E. At the time of the investigation, the soil could be seen stained about 40 yds x 15 yds. Specific conductivity measurements were taken in the area of the affected soil with a range of 2.1 mS/cm to 4.0 mS/cm. 4.0 mS/cm is the upper limit of the Department's meter. Specific conductivity was also measured in UNT to Ramsey with a reading of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Ramsey run pH measured 7.6. At the time of the measurements, UNT to Ramsey Run appeared unaffected by the spill. PGE had a contractor there removing the contaminated soil with Moody and Associates delineating the spill area on Moore Rd. Ext. The contaminated soil was excavated off Pad E and placed on plastic to be loaded in a roll back dumpster. The release of production fluid is considered a violation since the estimated volume is over 42 gallons. PGE is required to go through the Act 2 process.

Comments: On 03/25/26 an incident inspection of the GH2 Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 03/25/26. (CTS #396140) Background:On 03/25/26 CNX self-reported a release of production fluid. On 03/25/26 I spoke to Bruce Carpenter of CNX to acquire additional details about the spill. Mr. Carpenter informed me the spill was the result of a leaking pipe union that carried produced fluid to the bulk tanks and that the approximate volume of the spill was estimated to be roughly 20 gallons. No impacts to WoC were observed. Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a54 are being issued for the release of brine to the ground.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 962248
Permit API: 081-20531
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response from a notification from the operator that on July 18, 2022, an unknown volume of brine, mixed with oil and stormwater, had overflowed the secondary containment. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. Tobias excavation was also present on location as well as Creston Environmental. A coiled tubing unit and associated equipment was present on the pad on secondary containment. Damp areas and puddles were present on the north and south sides of the containment. Rick Hall said that the fluid made it off of the containment on both sides. On the north side of the containment the electrical conductivity (EC) in the puddles as measured by the Oakton meter ranged from 651 uS/cm to 3.16 mS/cm. On the south side of the containment each puddle I measured had an EC of greater than 19.99 mS/cm. Toward the end of my inspection, personnel on location had removed a portion of the containment berm on the north side and pulled back the liner approximately 15 feet which revealed that the gravel under the containment was damp. I would estimate the area visibly impacted by the release at approximately 600 square feet.Rick Hall said that the coiled tubing crew should be done by Thursday, July 21st, and then the containment would be removed from the pad surface. Screening of the pad surface where the containment was present would occur at that time, according to Rick Hall. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation.Violations noted.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 6/15/2023
Comments: This was an inspection performed following a report that the operator had a leaking brine tank on the Enis Lease. I inspected all three tank batteries on this lease.This well is producing and is equipped with a gas powered pumpjack. No spills or leaks are noted at the well. There is a tank battery near the well with two 210 barrel stock tanks contained. There is a buried brine tank across the access road in a wooded area. It appears that there has been an ongoing small leak in the tank, which has allowed brine to leak out into the soil. Impacted soil is apparent ~35 linear feet from the tank, at the base of a small hill. A check with a soil EC meter showed conductivity ranging from 1.5 to 5 mS in the soil. The liquid, along with deer activity, has stripped away vegetation from a 10x15 foot area. The water does not appear to have traveled much further than this and does not appear to be a threat to enter the waters of the Commonwealth.After this visit, I called the operator and he came to the site a little later to look at it with me. He agreed that the tank appeared to be leaking. I suggested that the tank would need to be vacuumed out, removed from the ground and the impacted soils remediated. He said that he would be contacting a contractor immediately to begin this process. Continued followup will be done as necessary.

Comments: I performed an INCDT inspection upon notice of a release of produced water reported to the Department on the Abbott Pad. The weather at the time of inspection was overcast and about 31 degrees F. According to the spill notice, CID#338740, Steve Watson (Cabot Oil & Gas) notified DEP Answering Service who contacted Jonathan Ulanoski (NERO - ER). Jonathan notified Mike O'Donnell (Scranton Office - O&G) that on 12/12/18 Tetra (water transfer contractor) was disconnecting a section of the transfer line on the tank pad. While doing so, approximately 1-2 bbls of residual frac fluid from the line spilled off containment onto the tank pad surface. The spill was reported to the Department within the 2-hour reporting requirement at 5:50 pm. It was reported that at the time of the notification the spill area had been coned off, covered with plastic, and secured for the night. On 12/13/2018 remediation efforts were to be put into place. Resource Environmental will be overseeing all remediation activities. On 12/13/2018, I met with Abby Vogler and Christian Mondy from Resource Environmental. Prior to excavating the area impacted by the release, it was noted that the highest recorded conductivity at any of the screened sampling points was found to be 0.446 millisiemens. After excavation the highest reading in the affected area was 0.148 millisiemens . The excavation (Photo 4) was about 2-4 inches deep in an area about 25' x 25'. There were approximately 3-4 yards of pad material excavated into a rolloff container (Photo 5). I spoke with Herb Swiney, Contract Safety Consultant,on site as well, who stated the site was secured immediately after the release and a rolloff container was called for. The container was to arrive the following morning, 12/13/2018, and excavation started upon arrival. The site was reportedly covered overnight and due to the freezing conditions, the release stayed mostly surficial. By phone, I then spoke with Steve Watson, Cabot representative. He indicated that systematic random sampling for Act 2 would occur this afternoon, (December 13, 2018). The rolloff container would either go to Alliance or Keystone landfill. A report will be prepared detailing the sampling results. While onsite, I also performed a RTNC E&S inspection. The access road (Photo 7) and pad surfaces were solid and stable, as was the cut and fill slopes of the tank and well pads (Photos 6 and 8). The vegetation was visible through the snow and appeared to meet stabilization requirements. There were no erosional anomalies noted during the inspection. There are violations attached to this inspection.

Permit API: 015-21167
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Smithfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Nichols A (1H) well site located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 8/19/2024 at 1110 hours. The weather was 67 degrees F with cloudy skies. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours.This inspection was conducted to summarize site remediation efforts completed by Blackhill Energy after a release was reported to the DEP on 7/29/2024 and violations were cited in inspection report #3804993. Pad material/soils located within the excavation area today were field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 0.08 to 0.23mS/cm. No pooled fluids were located within the excavation area, however, pooled fluids on the pad surface near the excavation area were field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 155 to 275us/cm. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. On behalf of Blackhill Energy, Moody and Associates (Moody's) submitted a 15-day interim report and NOV (notice of violation) response to the DEP on 8/7/2024. The report is attached to this inspection via file and has been uploaded to eFACTS. The NOV response indicated that interim remedial actions and site characterization activities were initiated on 7/29/2024. The NOV response also indicated that impacted pad materials and soils with electrical conductivity readings above 1.0mS/cm were excavated and placed in a lined roll-off container. Moody's collected soil attainment samples for the PADEP brine list and Ethylene Glycol following the PADEP's systematic random sampling protocol. Due to the presence of foam released with the produced water, Ethylene Glycol was added to the analyte list. Blackhill Energy plans to submit a Statewide Health Standard Site Characterization and Final Report within 90 days.Violations cited on 7/29/2024 against API #015-21167 remain outstanding at this site from the previous release. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed.I departed the site at 1215 hours.

Comments: On 10/16/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 10/12/2023 (IR 3630018, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Paul Stiner of Diversified. On 10/12/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued as outstanding for the observed elevated conductivity and the access road condition. The following was observed during inspection on 10/16/2023:The operator had removed impacted soils within the bottom portion of the berm, adjacent to the valve of tank 4. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 1-6). The operator had placed the impacted soils within buckets that were dated (Photos 7, 8).Some soils were removed from the berm adjacent to tank 5. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 9, 10).Regarding the area behind tank 5, it appeared as though the area I initially discovered to have elevated readings, and the operator was not able to replicate my readings, displayed adequate readings on 10/16/23, most likely due to dilution from rain (Photos 11, 12). There was one reading of 3.29 m/S, however this area was small, approximately a 4 inch by 4 inch section (Photo 13). The operator is going to remove some soils from this area, which was marked with a brick (Photo 14). Due to the size of this area, no violation is being noted.The operator explained that the cause of the impacted berm was due to fluids reaching the ground during tank clean out (Photos 15, 16). It is highly recommended to place containment/grate to collect any residual fluids and prevent them from reaching the ground and berm during tank clean out.The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 17, 18). On 10/13/2023, I had emailed Daniel Frick of Diversified regarding the start time of repairs; Diversified is waiting on bids and can hopefully update me next week (from 10/13 email). As of 10/16/2023, there has not been an update. Also in this email, I had asked if the NOV response for IR 3620008, mentioning the removal of a 5 gallon bucket, was referring to the area under the valve of tank 4 instead of behind tank 5, which was then confirmed to be correct - the material was removed from under the valve. Due to the operator's effort to remediate the impacted areas and the impacted areas appearing in relatively good condition, the violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, and SWMA 301, regarding the release of production fluid, are being closed. Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a), regarding the access road, remain outstanding.

Comments: On February 5 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to IR 3641696.The findings are as follows:The site appears to be unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 12/12/23. The previously observed fine, light colored material, identified by operator representive Joel Greco as fine limestone material was observed again. The fine limestone material still appeared to be holding an excess amount of water resulting in the ground surrounding the production tank to be soft and not properly stabilized. On 12/13/2023 the Department spoke to Mr.Greco on the phone regarding the previously observed stabilization concerns with the material and Mr.Greco stated that the material would stabilize after it dries once, allowing it to compact. However, at the time of this inspection the fine limestone material has not stabilized and is still soft, resulting in improper stabilization which increases the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. Based on today's inspection, violations associated with the spill remain open as it does not appear the operator has complied with the Department's Spill Policy at this time. Additional violations are being issued for improper site stabilization.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#302235). This well is located approximately 1,444' from the complainants water well. The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. The well is equipped for production and is currently producing. The well is equipped with a required check valve. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation and are current. As part of the investigation 4 slam bar holes were placed into the ground in the cardinal directions approximately 6" to 1' from the well-head and approximately 3' deep to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II gas meter which was calibrated on 05/06/2024 was used to take the soil gas readings. A soil gas reading of 4% LEL on the North slam bar hole, 32% LEL on the East, 2% LEL on South, and 10% LEL on West was observed at the time of inspection. As a result of the soil gas readings around this well the following violations are being cited: Violation: 78.73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater. Violation: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. Violation: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. Violation: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. At this time, the Department is requesting that the operator conduct an investigation to determine the source of methane around the well.

Permit API: 117-22060
Unconventional: Yes

Comments: Follow-up inspection to assess overall conditions. I met with Rockdale company man Jim Tracey upon my arrival on location. Jim informed me that they were drilling on the 9H well. A sump has been installed near the northeast corner of the pad. A sump pump is in the sump and a hose is connected to it which leads to a half round tank nearby on containment. The electrical conductivity (EC) within the sump is 8.7 mS/cm. A very small puddle on the pad surface between the diesel based mud containment and the upright diesel tank containment has an EC of 5.83 mS/cm. A small sump is also present in the northeast basin. The EC in this sump is 0.897 mS/cm. No water was flowing out of the NE basin outfall. A trash pump is staged near the NE basin and has hoses leading from the sump and to the half round tank near the northeast corner of the pad. A metal piece has been added to the exhaust side of the blender fan to direct the air from the fan downward onto secondary containment. EC of fluid on this area of secondary containment is 2.36 mS/cm. Don Haury, Motor Hand with Patterson, Rockdale's drilling contractor, stated that they hadn't been using any additives since 8/19/19 when they drilled to total depth (TD) on the 10H well. They started to add additives again during this inspection as they were preparing to drill with diesel based mud again. Mr. Haury stated that the additives were Calcium Chloride, Lime, and a black powdery substance that he couldn't remember the name of. The blue upright tank near the northeast corner of the pad remains in insufficient containment. Violations noted. Violations pending sample results.
